arxiv-2011-05970.title: Transformers for One-Shot Visual Imitation
arxiv-2011-05970.creator: Sudeep Dasari, Abhinav Gupta
arxiv-2011-05970.description: Abstract Humans are able to seamlessly visually imitate others, by inferring their intentions and using past experience to achieve the same end goal. In other words, we can parse complex semantic knowledge from raw video and efficiently translate that into concrete motor control. Is it possible to give a robot this same capability?

arxiv-2205-04727.title: Spectra of a Gapped Quantum Spin Liquid with a Strong Chiral Excitation on the Triangular Lattice
arxiv-2205-04727.creator: Ta Tang, Brian Moritz, Thomas P. Devereaux
arxiv-2205-04727.description: Abstract While a quantum spin liquid (QSL) phase has been identified in the J 1 J_{1} - J 2 J_{2} Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice via numerical calculations, debate persists about whether or not such a QSL is gapped or gapless, with contradictory conclusions from different techniques.

arxiv-2308-05052.title: Designing Cellular Networks for UAV Corridors via Bayesian Optimization This work was supported by the Spanish Research Agency through grant PID2021-123999OB-I00, CEX2021-001195-M, and the “Ramón y Cajal” program, by the UPF-Fractus Chair, and by Generalitat Valenciana, Spain, through grants CIDEGEN
arxiv-2308-05052.creator: Mohamed Benzaghta ⋆ , Giovanni Geraci ⋆ , David López-Pérez ♯ , and Alvaro Valcarce ♭
arxiv-2308-05052.description: Abstract As traditional cellular base stations (BSs) are optimized for 2D ground service, providing 3D connectivity to uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires re-engineering of the existing infrastructure. In this paper, we propose a new methodology for designing cellular networks that cater for both ground users and UAV corridors based on Bayesian optimization.

arxiv-2401-02987.title: Has your Pre-trained Model Improved? A Multi-head Posterior Based Approach
arxiv-2401-02987.creator: Prince Aboagye, Yan Zheng, Junpeng Wang, Uday Singh Saini, Xin Dai, Michael Yeh, Yujie Fan, Zhongfang Zhuang, Shubham Jain, Liang Wang, Wei Zhang
arxiv-2401-02987.description: Abstract The emergence of pre-trained models has significantly impacted Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Computer Vision to relational datasets. Traditionally, these models are assessed through fine-tuned downstream tasks. However, this raises the question of how to evaluate these models more efficiently and effectively.

arxiv-2407-17213.title: Spectrum-Informed Multistage Neural Network: Multiscale Function Approximator of Machine Precision
arxiv-2407-17213.creator: Jakin Ng, Yongji Wang, Ching-Yao Lai
arxiv-2407-17213.description: Abstract Deep learning frameworks have become powerful tools for approaching scientific problems such as turbulent flow, which has wide-ranging applications. In practice, however, existing scientific machine learning approaches have difficulty fitting complex, multi-scale dynamical systems to very high precision, as required in scientific contexts.

arxiv-2502-03098.title: Simple and efficient computational strategies for calculating orbital energies and pair-orbital energies from pCCD-based methods
arxiv-2502-03098.creator: Seyedehdelaram Jahani, Somayeh Ahmadkhani, Katharina Boguslawski, Paweł Tecmer
arxiv-2502-03098.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Seyedehdelaram Jahani, Somayeh Ahmadkhani, Katharina Boguslawski, Paweł Tecmer. We introduce affordable computational strategies for calculating orbital and pair-orbital energies in atomic and molecular systems. Our methods are based on the pair Coupled Cluster Doubles (pCCD) ansatz and its orbital-optimized variant. The computed orbital and pair-orbital energies are then subsequently used to approximate ionization potentials (IP), electron affinities (EA), the resulting charge gaps, double ionization potentials (DIP), and double electron affinities (DEA).

pmc-10636873.title: Establishing the health and wellbeing needs of mining host community in Brazil, Chile and Peru: a mixed-method approach to identify priority areas for action to help communities meet their SDG3 targets
pmc-10636873.creator: Brian Rice, Ana Maria Buller, Delia Boccia, Cesar Bazan, Rafael Miranda, Ximena Cea, Rodrigo Laro, Miguel Fontes, Rosalie Hayes, Mariken de Wit, Daniel J. Carter, Alexandra Plowright, Matthew Chadwick, Mitzy Gafos

In 2018, Anglo American plc published their Sustainable Mining Plan, containing a goal for improving health and wellbeing aligned with the Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG3) targets.

pmc-11429034.title: Music Listening as Exploratory Behavior: From Dispositional Reactions to Epistemic Interactions with the Sonic World
pmc-11429034.creator: Mark Reybrouck, Piotr Podlipniak, David Welch, Jerrell Cassady
pmc-11429034.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Listening to music can span a continuum from passive consumption to active exploration, relying on processes of coping with the sounds as well as higher-level processes of sense-making. Revolving around the major questions of “what” and “how” to explore, this paper takes a naturalistic stance toward music listening, providing tools to objectively describe the underlying mechanisms of musical sense-making by weakening the distinction between music and non-music.

pmc-11438890.title: HSP90 promotes tumor associated macrophage differentiation during triple-negative breast cancer progression
pmc-11438890.creator: Lingjia Hong, Manami Tanaka, Masato Yasui, Mariko Hara-Chikuma
pmc-11438890.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) originating from monocytes are crucial for cancer progression; however, the mechanism of TAM differentiation is unclear. We investigated factors involved in the differentiation of monocytes into TAMs within the tumor microenvironment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). We screened 172 compounds and found that a heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) inhibitor blocked TNBC-induced monocyte-to-TAM differentiation in human monocytes THP-1.

pmc-11504270.title: Neglected Achilles Tendon Rupture Repair with Gastrosoleus Turn Down Flap: A Case Report
pmc-11504270.creator: Jafri Hasan, Wintang Dayinta Tanaya Hutami
pmc-11504270.description: Introduction:The most prevalent tendon rupture in the lower extremities is an achilles tendon rupture. Adults in their third to fifth decades of life are the ones who sustain the injury most frequently. The optimal method for treating these ruptures is not generally agreed upon in the literature.

pmc-12398959.title: Adherence to EAT-Lancet diet and odds of irritable bowel syndrome and functional dyspepsia: the Isfahan functional disorders (ISFUN) study
pmc-12398959.creator: Asma Salari-Moghaddam, Awat Feizi, Parisa hajihashemi, Alireza Ani, Hamidreza Roohafza, Peyman Adibi
pmc-12398959.description: BackgroundNo study has been conducted to investigate the association between adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet and odds of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and functional dyspepsia (FD). This cross-sectional study was aimed to assess the association between adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet and odds of IBS and FD.

pmc-12682542.title: Dosimetric impact of bladder volume variation on online adaptive radiotherapy for cervical cancer based on cone-beam computed tomography and clinical management strategies
pmc-12682542.creator: Yingnan Qi, Xuemei Chen, Feng Chi, Zhanlin Chen, Yu Luo, Senkui Xu, Yilin Wang, Lintao Shang, Tong Wang, Xiuying Mai, Yaoyao Lin, Weizheng Zheng, Yunfei Feng, Foping Chen, Xiaobo Jiang
pmc-12682542.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundDuring cervical cancer radiotherapy, unstable bladder volume can compromise target accuracy and increase radiation exposure to organs at risk (OARs). Although online adaptive radiotherapy (ART) can correct for interfractional variations, intrafractional bladder filling may still lead to dose deviations.

pmc-12722411.title: Early Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting After Bariatric Surgery: A Study of 8426 Patients from the Swedish Perioperative Registry (SPOR)
pmc-12722411.creator: Jakob Walldén, Mattias Larsson, Antonio Moraitis, Sandra Ahlqvist, Yucel Cengiz, Tomi Myrberg, Helena Nyström, Magnus Hultin
pmc-12722411.description: BackgroundThe reported incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) after laparoscopic bariatric surgery is up to 60–80%. Hower, studies are limited, and larger studies are warranted. As PONV is usually evaluated in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU), studying early PONV can be a valuable tool for exploring risk and associated factors for PONV.

pmc-13044415.title: Urban malaria vector dynamics in Accra, Ghana
pmc-13044415.creator: Abdul Rahim Mohammed Sabtiu, Yaw Akuamoah-Boateng, Christopher Mfum Owusu-Asenso, Anisa Abdulai, Isaac Kwame Sraku, Daniel Kodjo Halou, Richard Tettey Doe, Emmanuel Nana Boadu, Sebastian Kow Egyin Mensah, Judith Dzifa Azumah, Sarkodie Adu-Barima, Lourees Esi Awotwe, Alberta Walker, Stephina Adjoa Ya
pmc-13044415.description: Urban malaria is an emerging challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, driven by unplanned urbanization, irrigation, and vector adaptation; yet data on urban vectors, their diversity and malaria transmission potential are limited. We assessed Anopheles gambiae s.l. abundance, species composition, and behavior in Accra, Ghana, during dry and rainy seasons of 2022 to 2024 across fifteen sites representing different socioeconomic settings.

pmc-13343868.title: Advances in electroacupuncture for perioperative neurocognitive disorders: mechanisms and clinical evidence
pmc-13343868.creator: Shirong Wei, Sitong Zhou, Junwen Tu, Tong Zhi, Yungong Wang, Qihong Shen, Chaobo Ni, Ming Yao, Huadong Ni
pmc-13343868.description: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), including postoperative delirium, delayed neurocognitive recovery, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction, are common complications in older surgical patients and are associated with impaired recovery, reduced quality of life, and increased postoperative morbidity. Current management remains largely supportive and preventive, and effective targeted therapies are still lacking.
